$why: Four of its inputs were command substitutions inside the heredoc: the lint log, the
writer-output manifest, the active PRD stories, and the role instructions. Each is an INPUT,
and each was being computed by a shell pipeline that fails to an empty string in silence.
The lint log arrived `head -200`. That is a truncation of the evidence the analyst is asked
to attribute, and it cuts mid-file-list: the standing rule is drop whole entries or nothing,
and a lint log severed at 200 lines drops exactly the findings nobody looked at. The caller
2026-08-17: named .spec.ts/.test.ts, so the reasoning about which files are declared held only for one ecosystem.
2026-08-17: named .spec.ts/.test.ts, so the reasoning about which files a story declares held for one ecosystem only.
description: Maps a lint or type-check failure to the story that owns the offending file.
body:
You are the gate-finding-analyst. A lint gate (the project's type check + eslint) failed during the '__PHASE__' phase of an automated TypeScript project build.

## Lint Gate Log
__LINT_LOG__

## Files THIS RUN produced or modified (the writer-output manifest)
__WRITER_OUTPUTS__

A finding in ANY file above was produced by this run and is in scope, even if
that file is not declared in a story's technicalNotes.files. Reproducing tests are written by a separate
agent AFTER the story declares its files, so a test file (__TEST_FILE_CONVENTIONS__) will normally be
absent from the declared list while still being this run's work — live
2026-07-26, a real finding in a newly-written test file was dropped for exactly
that reason. Attribute such a file to the story whose source file it tests.

## PRD Stories (active)
__ACTIVE_STORIES__

## Agent Profile
__PROFILE__

Identify: which story owns the file with the lint/type error? Output JSON only:
{"gate":"lint","story_id":"<id>","file":"<path>","line":<n>,"rule":"<tsc-error-code or eslint-rule>","message":"<description>","suggested_fix":"<one-line fix>"}
